extracted.intended_audience: scholars and students of history_of_science and philosophy_of_science; readers of Baconian methodology
extracted.subtask_description: Index entries and brief commentary summarizing Francis Bacon's methodological standards for investigation: induction, experiment design, types of instances, natural history compilation, and rules of exclusion used to discover forms and causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induction (Inductio/Inductio spes unica)
rubrics_metrics.description: Induction is essential to forming clear and adequate notions and true propositions; Bacon's inductio is to be new, elaborated, and applied to all sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Induction must separate, reject, and exclude (debebit separare, rejicere, excludere). It is not perfect until it rests in affirmative (non perfecta priusquam in affirmativa requiescat). The inductive logic admits great elaboration and is applicable to all sciences. (Entries: Inductio, Induction, Inductio spes unica, Inductive and Deductive Methods.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of Inductive and Deductive Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Inductive and deductive methods have a true relation: induction provides the basis for clear notions and axioms, while deduction builds upon them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Their proper relation and balance differ by science and requires attention (see 'Inductive and Deductive Methods, true relation of', 'their relation in different sciences').

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of Exclusions (Exclusions/Exclusiones)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use method(s) of exclusion to eliminate alternatives and narrow down causes and forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions are used repeatedly (222, 258, 309-10, 324, 327, 355-6, 362-3, 396-403, 413, 416, 418-19). The method of exclusions is explicitly part of inductive procedure and of finding forms (see 'Exclusions, Method of').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and Force of Negative Instances (Negativae instantiae)
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative instances carry significant evidential weight and should be used to refute or limit generalizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index notes 'Negativae instantiae major est vis' — negative instances have greater force. See also the many listed 'instantiae' types and the advice to reject/generalize only after proper exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Instances/Instances and Tables (Instantiae; Tabulae)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and classify many different kinds of instances (instantiae) and organize them in tables to discover forms and causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index enumerates many classes: instantiae praeorogativae (solitariae, migrantes, ostensivae, clandestinae, constitutivae, conformes, monodicae, deviantes, limitaneae, potestatis, comitatus et hostiles, subjunctivae, foederis, crucis, divortii, lampadis/ informationis primae, januae, citantes, viae, supplementi, persecutantes/vellicantes, and practical instances such as virgae/radii, curriculi, quanti, luctae, innuen^es, polychrestae, magicae). It also references comparison of instances/tables with Mill's methods and 'Instantiarum comparentia'. Use appropriate instance-types (including praeorogative instances) as methodological tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment vs Mere Observation (Experiment advantage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments are to be preferred to mere observation because they allow controlled inquiry and the testing of causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry: 'Experiment, advantage of over mere observation' and related remarks (Experiment, Experimentation). The text highlights designed experiment's superiority and necessity for establishing causal relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of Experiments (Experimenta qualia excogitanda sunt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments should be carefully devised to be illuminating and fruitful, not merely showy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes seeking 'experimenta lucifera et fructifera' (experiments that give light and fruit) and avoiding merely 'lucifera non fructifera' (showy but unfruitful). Also consult lists of practical, magical, and mathematical instances for appropriate experiment types (Instantiae practicae, magicae, mathematicae).

rubrics_metrics.name: Five Faults of Experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that Bacon enumerated five specific faults of experimentation which undermine reliable experimental practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index note: 'Experimentation, five faults of, enumerated by Bacon, 258-61.' While the faults are not listed in the index itself, the entry flags that experimenters must avoid these enumerated faults (see referenced pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Historia Naturalis (Experimental History) as Foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Build a copious, verified Historia Naturalis (natural history) that records many facts, including humble and small items—this is the basis of natural philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries emphasize that Historia Naturalis is too narrow so far and must be colligenda (collected) and verified ('non adhuc debitis modis exquisita', 'colligenda est', 'sua non satis copiosa et verificata'). It should include 'res etiam viles' and serve as 'basis philosophiae naturalis' and 'opus regium'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for Forms (Formae inquisitio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate the true forms (formae) of things as the foundation both for knowledge and for operation; forms may be sought by negatives and by instances constitutive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple entries: 'Formae... per negatives investigandae', 'per instantias constitutivas inve-niuntur particulariae formae', 'Formae... sunt ipsissimae res.' The index stresses the importance of discovering primary forms and their role in operation ('eas scire fundamentum tam ad sciendum quam ad operandum').

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of Compound Bodies by Reason and True Induction
rubrics_metrics.description: When dealing with compound bodies, separate components by rational analysis and true induction to reveal their constituent forms and causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry: 'corponim separatio facienda est per rationem et inductionem veram, 355.' This is a methodological rule for decomposing complex phenomena before induction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of Idols (Idola mentis/humanae)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and guard against idols of the mind (idola tribus, specus/cave, fori, theatri) which mislead inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: 'Idola mentis humanae' and subdivisions (tribus, specus, fori, theatri) with many references. The index highlights the centrality of overcoming cognitive biases in scientific method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notions and Definitions (Notiones primae)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary notions must be properly abstracted from sensory impressions; avoid vague, ill-terminated notions that mislead science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries warn: 'Notiones primae ab impressionibus sensuum male abstrahuntur, et vagae sunt nee bene terminatae' and note the necessity of adequate definition and the role of induction in constituting clear notions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of Nature (Interpretatio naturae)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation of nature is a mental work that begins from sense and leads to vindemiatio (first gleaning) and further inquiry toward forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: 'Interpretatio naturae... quid sit', 'Interpretatio naturae opus mentis verum et naturale', 'inchoata... vindemiatio prima, 404 sqq.', 'a sensu incipit, 490, 515.' Treat interpretation as structured, starting from observation and instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and Handling irregularities (Exceptiones / regularum generalium)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address exceptions to general rules carefully; regular general rules must be tested against exceptions and handled via exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index notes how antiquity handled exceptions ('Exceptiones, quomodo eas tractaverunt antiqui'), and 'regularum generalium, 442, 452'. Use exclusions and negative instances to manage exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Privileged Instances (Instantiae praeorogativae)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ privileged or praeorogative instances (lampadis, constitutivae, crucis, etc.) because they have special power to reveal forms and causal relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index lists praeorogative instance subtypes and their importance (lampadis/ informationis primae, constitutivae, crucis, januae, citantes, viae, supplementi, persecutantes, etc.). These are methodological tools singled out by Bacon for their evidential weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics and Natural Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics should terminate (provide tools for) physics but not generate physical knowledge; mathematics has a supporting role in natural philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry: 'Mathematica... terminare physicam, non generare debet' and notes on the relation of mathematics to natural philosophy (300-1, 358).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Mere Novelty and Superficiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Be wary of studies that pursue novelty for its own sake or superficial novelty; prefer advances that truly augment knowledge and utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: 'Novitatis studia, 232-3', warnings about 'experientia literata... fastidita', and remarks that many sciences remained superficial (medicine, music, optics) suggesting attention to depth and utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modi veritatis/inveniendi (Modes of discovery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize there are (at least) two modes of finding truth and multiple modes of operating on natural bodies; method selection matters to successful inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: 'Modi veritatem inveniendi duo, 200-2', 'Modi septem operandi super corpora naturalia, 570 sqq.' Use the appropriate mode(s) for the problem at hand.
